title: Design System: Woman of the Day

display.purpose: The hook on the sticker; printed twice in two inks.

headline.purpose: Her name on the museum label; the suggest-form heading.

title.purpose: Bio section headings and Sources, in deep riso blue.

body.purpose: The bio reading column, 65ch, oldstyle numerals.

plaque.purpose: The official record only: bold uppercase Atkinson; 0.8125rem on phones, 0.875rem from 640px.

detail.purpose: Field values, sources, further reading; captions and credits at 0.8125rem.

label.purpose: Field names and form labels in typed caps; buttons and stamps share the voice at 0.875-0.9375rem.

shadows.name: sticker-lift
shadows.purpose: The hook sticker at rest, lifting off the plaque.

shadows.name: sticker-flight
shadows.purpose: First frame of the slap, before the sticker lands.

motion.name: ease-slap
motion.purpose: Overshoot-free settle for the sticker slap and ink registration.

motion.name: slap
motion.value: 520ms ease-slap: scale 1.14 rotate -6deg -> scale 0.985 rotate -1.6deg (55%) -> scale 1 rotate -2deg
motion.purpose: The sticker lands once at load on the first entry; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: register
motion.purpose: The yellow pass settles into its fixed misregistration.

motion.name: button-fill
motion.purpose: Yellow hover fill on typed buttons.

motion.name: sticker-tip
motion.purpose: Submit button tips -1deg and lifts 2px on hover.

textures.name: grain
textures.value: var(--grain): SVG fractal noise, baseFrequency .9, 240px tile, opacity .16

textures.name: grain-ink
textures.value: var(--grain-ink): SVG fractal noise, baseFrequency .55, 180px tile, opacity .5, multiply

textures.name: riso-halftone

shareImage.notes: Satori render of masthead, yellow rule, plaque and sticker. Without blend modes it prints the inks' overprints literally: hook in overprint navy (#002284), yellow ghost over pink as #ff4100, plaque border #9a988f. These are share-card-only simulations, not palette tokens.

narrative.overview:
Every surface is a cheap, loud print job pasted over something official. A grey institutional plaque states the record as the institutions kept it; a fluorescent riso sticker is slapped across it, askew, and says what really happened. Below that sits a museum label typed in Courier with ruled fields, and then a calm reading column. The anger lives in the printed objects (sticker, stamps, overprinted ink); the reading itself is quiet, because the anger has to rest on sourced fact.

The material is newsprint: off-white paper with a faint fibre grain, three spot inks (fluorescent pink, riso blue, yellow) that multiply where they overlap and land a few pixels out of register. Photographs are never shown raw. Each real photo is screened twice, once per ink, and overprinted. Depth is physical, not interface depth: a sticker lifts off the plaque, a stamp sits flat in the paper. Light theme only, by binding brief.

Density is that of a printed broadsheet column on a phone: one story, top to bottom, with heavy ink rules between sections rather than cards.
keyCharacteristics: Off-white grained paper; three spot inks that overprint with multiply and misregister by 2-3px.
The plaque-and-sticker pair: official grey record overruled by a pink sticker rotated -2deg.
Courier Prime museum-label fields with hairline rules for every fact, date, source and credit.
Le Murmure for display only; Atkinson Hyperlegible for anything read at length.
Real photos as two-ink halftone duotones; no photo means the name printed twice in two inks.
Rubber stamps carry state (fallback, fuzzy date, draft, received).

rules.name: The Spot Ink Rule
rules.body: Colour comes only from the three inks and their deep text-safe forms. No smooth gradients (a hard-stop band, like the highlighter on a targeted source, is ink, not a gradient), no tints between inks, no fourth hue. When inks meet, they multiply.

rules.name: The Text-Safe Ink Rule
rules.body: Pink and blue at full fluorescence are grounds, marks and display type over pink; any colour carrying small text uses the deep form (pink-deep, blue-deep) to hold WCAG AA on paper.

rules.name: The Official Grey Rule
rules.body: Plaque grey belongs to the official record. Nothing that speaks for her is ever set on grey.

rules.name: The Headlines-Only Rule
rules.body: Le Murmure is for the hook, names, section headings and the sticker button. It never sets a sentence meant to be read at length, a label or a number field.

rules.name: The Evidence Is Typed Rule
rules.body: Dates, places, sources, credits, source marks and stamps are Courier Prime. If it is something a reader might check, it is typed.

rules.name: The Only Stickers Lift Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is a piece of stock pasted on top". Printed ink never lifts.

rules.name: The Grain Everywhere Rule
rules.body: The paper carries a faint fibre grain; ink solids carry a heavier mottled grain blended by multiply. No flat digital fills for the sticker, and no texture behind the reading column beyond the paper's own.

dos: Do print colour as ink: pink, blue and yellow only, overlapping with multiply and offset 2-3px out of register.
Do put the official record on plaque grey and overrule it with a pink sticker rotated -2deg, pulled up over the plaque's lower half.
Do set every checkable fact (dates, places, sources, credits) in Courier Prime with hairline rules.
Do keep the bio at 1.125rem / 1.65 in Atkinson Hyperlegible, 65ch max, on the paper's own grain only.
Do render every photo as the two-ink halftone, and print the name in two inks when there is no photo.
Do carry state with a tilted, worn rubber stamp in deep blue or deep fuchsia.
Do use deep pink and deep blue for any small text in colour; fluorescent pink and blue stay grounds and marks.
Do separate sections with a 2px press-black rule and generous print-like space (96px).
donts: Don't add a dark theme; the world is light paper only.
Don't use Le Murmure for body text, labels or fields.
Don't put texture, ink solids or colour behind the reading column.
Don't show a raw photo, an AI-generated image, a mascot or a cute doodle.
Don't use cream paper with a serif, or terracotta.
Don't introduce cards, rounded containers or interface shadows; only pasted stock lifts.
Don't set anything that speaks for her on plaque grey.
